4: Today's science lesson is the human body, and Maya has brought a giant poster. She points at the shoulder, the elbow, the knee, and asks the class to touch each one. Kili tries to follow: he has got wings instead of arms, no knees that anybody can see, and a tongue that nobody has ever noticed. Has he got a beard? Certainly not. What has YOUR body got? Point, name it and learn the map of yourself!
5: New timetable, team! Ingrid reads it out loud: maths before break, science after lunch, art on Tuesday and music on Friday afternoon. Diego groans at history and cheers at geography, because he wants to be a reporter and reporters need maps. On Wednesday there is no PE, and that is officially the worst news of the week. What subjects have YOU got today? Read your timetable and say it!
6: Atchoo! Oliver has got a cold and the concert is on Friday. You should drink hot lemon and honey, says Kili, who is not a doctor but has strong opinions. You shouldn't sing tonight, you should sleep. Oliver has also got a headache and, he thinks, a temperature. He takes the medicine and goes to bed at eight — a world record. What should you do when you're ill?
7: Report from the school kitchen! Diego investigates today's mystery: who finished the honey? There is some butter, there is a lot of flour and there are two boxes of cereal, but the honey jar is empty. How much jam is left? Only a little. How many eggs are there? Six. Maya writes the list for tomorrow while Diego keeps interviewing suspects. Countable or uncountable? Count what you can!
8: Expedition dinner tonight — pizza! Oliver, wash your hands, says Ingrid, taking charge. Have we got any cheese? Yes, we've got some. Have we got any mushrooms? No, we haven't got any, so we'll use olives and onion instead. Put the tomato on first, then the cheese, then everything else. Into the oven for twelve minutes! What do YOU put on your pizza? Give the instructions!
9: Welcome to Maya's new flat! The lift is broken, so there are ninety-two stairs between the gate and the front door — she has counted them. There is a small balcony with three plants above the street, a basement full of bicycles below, and from the roof you can see the whole city. Where is the light switch? Behind the door. Describe YOUR home: what is above, below and next to it?
10: Breaking news: Kili's lost-and-found box is completely FULL. Whose scarf is this? It's Ingrid's. Whose notebook is this? Not mine — it's his. Diego holds up a very strange hat and nobody claims it: it isn't ours, it isn't theirs, and it certainly isn't hers. Kili keeps it for himself. Whose things are lost in your classroom? Ask around and give them back!
11: Today Diego is interviewing real heroes. The firefighter climbs ladders and carries heavy equipment. The journalist writes stories and asks difficult questions. The engineer designs bridges, the dentist looks after our teeth, the pilot flies to twelve countries a month and the waiter remembers thirty orders without writing them down. What does YOUR family do? Interview someone and report back!
12: One day I'll play my songs in a huge stadium, says Oliver, with a spoon as a microphone. Maya is more scientific: I'll be a scientist, I'll study the oceans and I won't work in an office. Oliver won't stop singing, that much is certain. Some dreams come true, some change, and both are fine. What will YOU be when you grow up? Say it out loud — the future starts here!
13: Mission: cross the whole city in one hour using four kinds of transport! Ingrid and Diego go by tram to the centre, by bicycle along the river, by train from the platform at ten past four, and finally by taxi because they are late. They never touch the motorway, which Diego says is cheating anyway. Fifty-eight minutes — mission accomplished. How do you get to school? By bus, by bike, on foot? Plan your own city mission!
14: Kili has to deliver a letter to the new museum, and he has never been there. Go straight on to the end of this street, says Maya, then turn left at the bank, go past the bakery, along the river and over the old bridge. The museum is on your right. Kili flies over everything in ninety seconds, which is cheating. Can YOU give directions to a stranger? Try it!
15: Sports report by Diego! Our school volleyball team won the regional final on Saturday. We play volleyball and football, we go skating and snowboarding in winter, and we do gymnastics on Thursdays. Oliver went sledging last year and still talks about it. There is a race next month, and the whole school is training. What sports do YOU play, go or do? Get the verb right!
16: When the lights went out at the sports centre, everybody was doing something. Ingrid was practising her jump. Maya was swimming in the pool, and she didn't notice for a whole minute. Somebody was blowing a whistle in the dark and two children were laughing in the changing room. Nobody was scared — well, almost nobody. What were YOU doing at eight o'clock yesterday?
17: Oliver is writing a song with a verse for every month of the year. January is cold and quiet, in February there is a school party, in March the snow melts. April rhymes with nothing useful. In August everybody is away, and in October the wind returns. His birthday is on the ninth of June, so June gets the best verse. When is YOUR birthday? Add your month to the song!
18: The expedition timetable is strict, Diego! Breakfast at quarter past seven, not half past. We leave at quarter to eight. The museum opens at midday and closes at midnight — no, that can't be right, says Ingrid, checking again. Diego is always five minutes late and always has a good reason. Are you early or late? Look at the clock and say the exact time!
19: Look at those black clouds over the sea! Kili, come inside! Last winter there was a terrible storm here: the lightning lit up the whole bay, the thunder shook the windows and the fog arrived so thick that Maya couldn't see the lighthouse from her door. There was ice on the path and, later, a small flood in the basement. What was the worst weather YOU remember?
20: Museum challenge with Diego and Maya! This box is made of wood and it is three hundred years old. That ring is made of metal, this window is made of glass, and these old toys are made of paper and wool. The modern chair is made of plastic and nobody is impressed by it at all. The guide asks one last question and Diego, for once, knows the answer. Look around your classroom: what is your table made of? Find five things and say it!
21: Camping weekend! Follow the path up the hill — the camp is next to the wood, near the waterfall you can hear from far away. There is a small island in the middle of the lake and there is a cave behind the rocks that Ingrid wants to explore immediately. There are no shops, no cars and no wifi, only stars and the sound of water. Oliver says it is the best night of the year. What is there in the countryside near YOUR home?
22: Quiz time with Maya! Which river is longer, the Amazon or the Nile? Which ocean is the deepest? Which is the widest bridge in the world? Kili answers everything with total confidence and gets almost everything wrong, but he says it so well that nobody argues. The longest, the deepest, the highest: the planet loves records. Which is the longest river in YOUR country?
23: What a strange dream! Oliver landed on a purple planet where the rivers ran upwards and the moons sang at night. What an enormous rocket! What a friendly alien! What terrible food! Maya listens and asks scientific questions that ruin everything, like: what were the stars made of? Describe something amazing with What a…! and tell your own strange dream.
24: Kili delivered a photo album to the wrong house, and Diego opened it by mistake. Inside there is a very unusual family: the mother has got long curly green hair, the father has got a short dark beard and only one eye, and the tall child has got straight fair hair down to the floor. They all look extremely happy. Describe the people in YOUR photos: what have they got?
25: A good expedition team needs all kinds of people, says Ingrid. Maya is clever and quiet, and she notices everything. Diego is friendly and never stops talking, which is useful in an interview. Oliver is brave on a stage and afraid of spiders. And Kili? Kili is not lazy — he is 'saving energy'. What are YOUR friends like? Describe their personality, not their face!
26: Today's big question for the whole school: have you ever met a famous person? Diego has interviewed a TV presenter, so he says yes, twice, and tells the story four times. Ingrid has never met anybody famous but she has flown in a helicopter, which she thinks is better. Have you ever eaten something really strange? Have you ever been on television? Ask ten people, count the answers and bring them to class!
27: Kili has just crashed into the window with today's mail. Again. He has already delivered nine letters this morning, but he hasn't finished yet — there are six more in his bag. Oliver has just written a new song, Ingrid has already read it, and nobody has told him yet that it sounds exactly like the last one. What have YOU just done? Say it before the moment passes!
28: Oliver fell asleep in the library because he practised until two in the morning. He was tired, so he used a dictionary as a pillow. Maya was hungry, so she ate his sandwich — because he wasn't looking. The class was bored, so the teacher changed the plan. Everyone was excited, because tomorrow is the trip. Say WHY things happen with because, and WHAT happens with so!
29: Kili always delivers the mail at eight, usually with a crash. He often forgets one letter and sometimes eats the biscuits that arrive by post. He never apologises. Ingrid usually gets up early and always checks the weather; Maya sometimes reads until midnight and is never late. How often do YOU do things? Put the word in the right place and describe your habits!
